comment: THE SNAPSHOT CONTRACT -- one derivation site for the payload the generator writes and the dashboard reads. packages/snapshot/src/codec.ts builds its encoder and decoder from wardColumns and facilityColumns AT MODULE LOAD, so neither the generator nor the dashboard contains a column list of its own. Landed in Stage 0 rather than Stage 1 because it depends on nothing in Stage 1 and it is the artefact whose late decision forces rework on both sides at once. Paths here are unbackticked where they name something a later stage builds.
why_pollCadenceSeconds_is_here: RELEASE GATE 2's latency clause, restated 2026-09-10, asserts that 'a client poll at the snapshot's own cadence reflects the new count'. The assertion is written against THIS CONSTANT, never against a wall-clock number in prose. 30 matches the CDN's s-maxage=30: polling faster asks the edge for a document it is contractually allowed to keep serving, so it buys nothing and costs requests. stale-while-revalidate=300 means a poll may still legitimately receive a payload up to five minutes old, which is why the original 'within 60 seconds' clause could not be met by this architecture and was restated rather than kept. ONE SOURCE: the constant is not also carried in the envelope, because a client that could disagree with the fixture is a second derivation site.

decisions.v_is_never_a_timestamp_aggregate: v is a monotonic run counter or a content hash. NEVER max(updated_at) or any aggregate over it. Migration 008 writes public.ward_public.updated_at = ws.updated_at, which is correct -- a duty-flag flip changes the DERIVED gate without changing the ward's own claim -- but it means a version derived from a timestamp aggregate WOULD NOT MOVE when an anaesthetist goes off duty. The snapshot would then keep publishing a theatre as open at exactly the moment the gate closed it. Recorded here as well as in the function because this is the file both sides read.
decisions.server_now_is_the_only_freshness_anchor: The server stamps updated_at and emits server_now. The client computes age from those two plus monotonic elapsed time since fetch. It NEVER reads a wall clock -- finding F3. A handset three hours fast is the case: it renders a fresh ward as a day old, or a day-old ward as fresh, with total confidence and no error anywhere.
decisions.the_snapshot_never_carries_duty_flags: Not anaesthetist, not obstetrician, not paediatrician, in any form. gated_by is the public reason and it is all the public gets. TWO REASONS, and the second is the one that will bite. First, a duty flag is a fact about a named individual's shift and the public has no business with it. Second, the F2 ESLint rule matches on IDENTIFIER NAMES -- /anaesthetist|obstetrician|paediatrician/i -- and this payload is arrays-of-arrays, which destroys names. `!f[3]` is invisible to that rule. Exposure is zero today because the payload carries only gated_by; the natural widening, 'show WHY it is closed in a tooltip', is exactly what reintroduces it, past a guard that can no longer see it. Written down because it is currently a property nobody had stated.
decisions.freshness_does_not_live_in_the_gate_pack: packages/gate has a specific identity: rules implemented TWICE, in SQL and TypeScript, pinned by a shared fixture in one test.each block. Freshness has exactly one derivation site by design -- the server never computes an age. Putting it in packages/gate invites the next contributor to write the SQL twin for symmetry, and the SQL twin of a freshness rule is `where updated_at > now() - interval '2 hours'`, which is the precise collapse scripts/lint_no_updated_at_filter.sh exists to ban.

why_the_golden_payload_has_a_gated_ward: The THEATRE row is accepting_effective=false with gated_by set and bed_count=2 -- beds exist and the gate closed the ward anyway. That is the shape a decoder gets wrong by rendering bed_count and ignoring the gate, and a golden payload of only happy rows would never catch it. Its updated_at is also two hours older than the facility's, so the freshness band under test is not always the fresh one.
